review_notes: Reviewed all 154 lines, including the character definitions, roots-of-unity maps, and their proofs. I also checked the analogous `AddChar.zmod_intCast` simp lemma and the downstream Fourier and L-series uses. The proposed simp attribute appears to give a useful cast-to-exponential normal form; I did not identify a competing rewrite in the inspected sources.

findings.excerpt:
lemma toCircle_intCast (j : ℤ) :
    toCircle (j : ZMod N) = exp (2 * π * I * j / N) := by
findings.problem: This cast-to-exponential formula is not a simp lemma, so routine expressions such as `ZMod.toCircle (j : ZMod N)` do not simplify to the explicit character value unless callers name the theorem. The neighboring `stdAddChar_coe` proof has to include `toCircle_intCast` explicitly, while an analogous `AddChar.zmod_intCast` formula in the Pontryagin duality source is marked `[simp]`.
findings.proposed_change: Consider marking `toCircle_intCast` with `@[simp]`, so `simp` normalizes `ZMod.toCircle (j : ZMod N)` to `exp (2 * π * I * j / N)`. Check the resulting simp behavior alongside `toCircle_natCast` before also annotating the natural-cast variant.
findings.benefit: Makes the explicit value available through ordinary simplification for integer-cast inputs and aligns this API with the analogous character formula. This can reduce manual theorem references in proofs while retaining the exponential expression as the normal form.

evidence.excerpt:
lemma toCircle_intCast (j : ℤ) :
    toCircle (j : ZMod N) = exp (2 * π * I * j / N) := by
stdAddChar (j : ZMod N) = exp (2 * π * I * j / N) := by simp [stdAddChar, toCircle_intCast]
@[simp] lemma zmod_intCast (x y : ℤ) : zmod n x y = exp (2 * π * (x * y / n)) := by
